messages.subject: Re: Dirichlet something <= 0
parts:
On Monday, April 27, 2015 at 11:39:16 PM UTC-4, Michael Henry Tessler wrote:
I get the following error (informational message) printed about 20 times and stan returns with no samples...

Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:
stan::prob::dirichlet_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): prior sample sizes[2] is -0.495263:0, but must be > 0!

That means xform_prits can be negative. I'm not really sure where you are going with these transformations but the logit() function inputs a number between 0 and 1 and outputs a real number. You may have meant inv_logit(), which is the inverse of that.

Ben

On Monday, April 27, 2015 at 8:39:16 PM UTC-7, Michael Henry Tessler wrote:
Hi there,

I've gone through removing bits from my model and I think I have it down to a minimal case (still, many lines of code, but the generative model is simple.

The gist of the model is to try to infer people's subjective probabilities about certain (highly esoteric) domains using 2 different behavioral measurements. The first, captured in ntdata, is where participants are asked to give an option from a set of 16 options. I model this as coming from a categorical. The second (which is where the problem lies), captured in bhdata, is where participants are asked to rate each of the 16 options. I take their ratings, normalize them so they add to 1, and model that as coming from a dirichlet. 

The model (inside .Rmd) and data are attached. I've run the model with just the ntdata half and it works fine. The problem, I believe, is with bhdata and with the dirichlet. I've also attached the full model (skyprior.stan.R), which is what I was using before I started pruning, in case you have a chance to take a look at this. This is my second model in STAN.
I get the following error (informational message) printed about 20 times and stan returns with no samples...

Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:
stan::prob::dirichlet_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): prior sample sizes[2] is -0.495263:0, but must be > 0!

If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,
but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified.
Rejecting proposed initial value with zero density.
